Speech recognition has come a long way over the last decade. Early systems needed careful dictation in a quiet room, and they still made many mistakes. Modern neural models listen to ordinary conversation, handle different accents, and produce punctuated text in a fraction of real time. This progress came from large amounts of training data, better architectures such as the conformer, and decoding methods that predict both tokens and their durations.
